prompt:
Build a closed-loop Simulink navigation model for a car-like mobile robot on a known two-dimensional binary occupancy map. Read MapMatrix, StartPose, GoalPose, ObstacleSafetyMargin, MinimumTurningRadius, MaxLinearVelocity, and MaxAngularVelocity from the MATLAB base workspace. The start and goal will be collision-free poses in the same reachable free-space component, and all scalar inputs will remain within their declared ranges.

MapMatrix is a known binary occupancy matrix with zero meaning free and one meaning occupied (unitless); StartPose and GoalPose are 1-by-3 real vectors ordered [x_m, y_m, heading_rad]; ObstacleSafetyMargin is a real scalar in [0.8, 1.3] m; MinimumTurningRadius is a real scalar in [2.0, 2.5] m; MaxLinearVelocity is a real scalar in [10, 16] m/s; and MaxAngularVelocity is a real scalar in [0.75, 0.9] rad/s.

The model must generate a collision-free global route, repeatedly produce a locally feasible trajectory from the current robot state, execute bounded linear and angular commands through a bicycle-kinematic plant, and feed the simulated pose back into local planning. It must respect the map, vehicle turning limit, speed limits, and obstacle margin. If a local solution becomes infeasible, the model must retain a useful feasible prefix, correct the command, or request a new global route instead of bypassing the constraint.

Use a vehicle footprint 4 m long and 2 m wide with a 1 m wheelbase. Run until the goal is reached or for at most 100 s. Reaching the goal requires actual position and heading proximity, not a timer or a declared success flag alone. This task uses a known static map; it does not require SLAM, raw sensor processing, moving-obstacle prediction, or high-fidelity wheel and terrain dynamics.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named robot_state, executed_command, and planner_state. robot_state has 5 channels in this order: x (m), y (m), heading (rad), linear velocity (m/s), and angular velocity (rad/s). executed_command has 2 channels: linear-velocity command (m/s) and angular-velocity command (rad/s). planner_state has 4 channels in this order: has reached goal, last feasible index, exit flag, and global replan request. Save the completed model as cand_XROBO07.slx in the submission directory and keep its latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XROBO07.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
